title: Algebra of Limits

mental_model.intuition: The limit of a sum is the sum of the limits, as long as both limits exist.
mental_model.description: You can split limits into smaller, easier pieces using basic algebra rules, just like distributing multiplication over addition.

explanation: The algebra of limits provides tools to simplify complex expressions. But these rules have conditions. You can only split a limit if the individual limits exist as real numbers. For quotients, you can only split them if the denominator's limit is non-zero.

derivation.goal: Evaluate the limit of (x^2 + 5x) as x approaches 2

steps.why: The limit of a sum is the sum of the limits.

predict.question: Is it safe to split this limit into two parts?

options.feedback: You can only split a limit if the individual limits exist as real numbers. Both these limits exist.

steps.why: Pull the constant 5 out of the second limit.

predict.question: What do you do with the constant 5?

options.feedback: A constant pulled out of a limit must be multiplied by the final limit value, not added.

steps.why: Add to get the final answer.

rules.statement: The limit of a sum is the sum of the limits, as long as both limits exist.
A constant number multiplied by a function can be pulled outside the limit sign.
When putting the value of the variable no longer causes division by zero, substitute the number and drop the limit sign.

common_mistakes.title: Quotient rule division by zero
common_mistakes.explanation: Students often split a limit into a fraction when the bottom limit is zero. You cannot split a limit into a fraction if the bottom limit is zero. Simplify the expression first.

recall_questions.q: Explain the limit sum rule in your own words, as if to a classmate.
recall_questions.answer: You can break a big limit into smaller limits and add them up, but only if each smaller limit actually goes to a real number.

recall_questions.q: When are you NOT allowed to use the quotient rule for limits?
recall_questions.answer: You cannot use the quotient rule when the limit of the denominator is exactly zero.

recall_questions.q: What must you do with a constant number pulled out of a limit?
recall_questions.answer: You must multiply it by the result of the limit.
